verses.zh: 我因锡安必不静默，为耶路撒冷必不息声，直到他的公义如光辉发出，他的救恩如明灯发亮。
verses.en: For the sake of Zion I will not be silent;for the sake of Jerusalem[NOTE:1] I will not be quiet,until her vindication shines brightly[NOTE:2] and her deliverance burns like a torch.
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
verses.commentary:
62:1 "Zion. . .Jerusalem" These are in a Hebrew parallel relationship. Jerusalem was built on seven hills.
Mount Zion was not the site of the Temple, but the location of David's palace and came to be a reference to the
whole city of Jerusalem.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MORIAH, SALEM, JEBUS, ZION, JERUSALEM

▣ The VERBS "be silent" (Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 364, KB 361)
and "be quiet" (Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 1052, KB 1641), both negated, are related to the positive
statement of Isa. 61:1.

The "I" could refer to the prophet or the Servant/Messiah (Deity breaks the silence mentioned in Isa. 42:14;
57:11; 64:12; 65:6). Obviously Isaiah 60-62 are a literary unit.

▣ "righteousness. . .salvation" These two words also are in a parallel relationship. Righteousness
speaks of the position and lifestyle of the people of God which results in their physical deliverance from their
enemies. In the OT the term "salvation" primarily refers to a physical deliverance, while in the NT the term refers
primarily to spiritual forgiveness and a standing before God. Zion's (cf. Isa. 61:10-11) new day has come and will
affect the whole world (cf. Isa. 62:2; 60:3)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT)

▣ "brightness. . .burning" Again the presence of YHWH is connected to light, as it was on Mt. Sinai
(cf. Exodus 19-20). See note at Isa. 60:1.

Israel was meant to be "the light" of YHWH to the darkness of paganism and fertility worship.
However, she was captured by them. The NT gives this same mission of revelation (i.e. Jesus is God's ultimate
Light, cf. John 1:4; 8:12; 12:35) and evangelism as the believers' task (cf. Matt. 5:14-16; 28:19-20; Luke 24:46-47; Acts 1:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LIGHT

SPECIAL TOPIC: DARKNESS

verses.zh: 列国必见你的公义；列王必见你的荣耀。你必得新名的称呼，是耶和华亲口所起的。
verses.en: Nations will see your vindication,and all kings your splendor.You will be called by a new namethat the Lord himself will give you.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “which the mouth of the Lord will designate.”
verses.commentary:
62:2 "The nations will see your righteousness" Israel was chosen by YHWH to be a witness to the entire
world to bring them to Himself (cf. Isa. 62:11; 52:10; 60:3; 61:6,11; 1 Pet. 2:5,9; Rev. 1:6). This is the true meaning
of the phrase "a kingdom of priests" (cf. Exod. 19:5-6).

▣ "And you will be called by a new name" The imparting of a new name implies the new age of the
Spirit. The new covenant is realized.

The term "new" (BDB 294 I) is used extensively in the second part of Isaiah to describe the
new day of righteousness.

- new things, Isa. 42:9; 48:6

- new song, Isa. 42:10 (cf. Rev. 5:9; 14:3)

- something new, Isa. 43:19 (cf. Rev. 3:12)

- new name, Isa. 62:2 (cf. Isa. 56:5)

- new heavens and a new earth, Isa. 65:17; 66:22 (cf. 2 Pet 3:13)

The "new" day (cf. Rev. 21:5) was, in reality, the day that God always wanted for humans, but
the Fall in Genesis 3 caused a terrible disruption! It is surely possible that the Bible's imagery of heaven is a
restored Garden of Eden (cf. Rev. 21:2).

SPECIAL TOPIC: OLD THINGS. . .NEW THINGS

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

SPECIAL TOPIC: EDEN

verses.zh: 你在耶和华的手中要作为华冠，在你　神的掌上必作为冕旒。
verses.en: You will be a majestic crown in the hand of the Lord,a royal turban in the hand of your God.
verses.commentary:
62:3 The Jerome Bible Commentary, vol. 1, p. 383, mentions that ancient eastern people
believed their gods wore a crown shaped like the city that worshiped them. If so, then this may be a cultural
allusion to this concept. This view depends on

- YHWH being the speaker of chapter 62

- how widespread this pagan concept was known

The Bible does use pagan imagery to describe and magnify YHWH. Four of many possible examples:

- "God of Heaven" in Nehemiah

- allusion to Persian Zoroastrian deity, Mal. 4:2

- allusion to the twelve signs of the zodiac in Rev. 12:1

- allusion to evil as a dragon

In Isa. 28:5 YHWH Himself is the crown of the covenant people. He is their glory, light, provision, protection, and victory!

In Zech. 9:16 the covenant people are the jewels in YHWH's crown.

▣ "in the hand of the Lord. . .in the hand of your God" Notice the parallelism.

- Lord (BDB 217) = YHWH, SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

- God (BDB 43) = Eloah, SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

The eternal, non-corporal Deity is described in human terms. We have no other option to describe God but

- human terms

- negations ‒ what He is not

- analogy ‒ what He is like

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

verses.zh: 你必不再称为「撇弃的」；你的地也不再称为「荒凉的」。你却要称为「我所喜悦的」；你的地也必称为「有夫之妇」。因为耶和华喜悦你，你的地也必归他。
verses.en: You will no longer be called, “Abandoned,”and your land will no longer be called “Desolate.”Indeed,[NOTE:1] you will be called “My Delight is in Her”[NOTE:2] and your land “Married.”[NOTE:3] For the Lord will take delight in you,and your land will be married to him.[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “for”; KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV “but.”
Hebrew חֶפְצִי־בָהּ (kheftsi vah), traditionally transliterated “Hephzibah” (so KJV, ASV, NIV).
Hebrew בְּעוּלָה (beʿulah), traditionally transliterated “Beulah” (so KJV, ASV, NIV).

That is, the land will be restored to the Lord’s favor and once again enjoy his blessing and protection. To indicate the land’s relationship to the Lord, the words “to him” have been supplied at the end of the clause.
verses.commentary:
62:4 "Forsaken (BDB 736 I). . .Desolate (BDB 1031)" This describes Israel's own interpretation of the Exile (i.e. these are their titles
for themselves). They felt they had been forsaken (cf. Isa. 49:14-21; 54:6-7) by YHWH and wondered if He would ever love them again (cf. v. 12).

▣ "My delight is in her" This is their true title! "Delight" may be the name "Hephzi-bah" (BDB 343, cf. 2 Kgs. 21:1). This is the
beginning of sustained imagery about YHWH as marriage partner (cf. Isa. 62:4-5). It is hard to describe an infinite
Holy Creator God, therefore, we have to use human analogies. It is common in the Bible to describe God as Father,
as husband, as near kinsman.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FATHERHOOD OF GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINSMAN REDEEMER

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

▣ "married" This can also be translated "Beulah" (BDB 127). Lines 4 and 5 may be the "new name" of Isa. 62:2c.

This VERB (BDB 127, KB 42) is used four times in Isa. 62:4-5.

- Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE, Isa. 62:4

- Niphal IMPERFECT, Isa. 62:4

- Qal IMPERFECT, Isa. 62:5

- same as #3

Obviously, marriage is a good analogy for biblical faith (cf. Eph. 5:22-33).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HUMAN SEXUALITY

verses.zh: 少年人怎样娶处女，你的众民（民：原文是子）也要照样娶你；新郎怎样喜悦新妇，你的　神也要照样喜悦你。
verses.en: As a young man marries a young woman,so your sons[NOTE:1] will marry you.As a bridegroom rejoices over a bride,so your God will rejoice over you.
notes: The Hebrew text has “your sons,” but this produces an odd metaphor and is somewhat incongruous with the parallelism. In the context (v. 4b, see also 54:5-7) the Lord is the one who “marries” Zion. Therefore several prefer to emend “your sons” to בֹּנָיִךְ (bonayikh, “your builder”; e.g., NRSV). In Ps 147:2 the Lord is called the “builder of Jerusalem.” However, this emendation is not the best option for at least four reasons. First, although the Lord is never called the “builder” of Jerusalem in Isaiah, the idea of Zion’s children possessing the land does occur (Isa 49:20; 54:3; cf. also 14:1; 60:21). Secondly, all the ancient versions support the MT reading. Thirdly, although the verb בָּעַל (baʿal) can mean “to marry,” its basic idea is “to possess.” Consequently, the verb stresses a relationship more than a state. All the ancient versions render this verb “to dwell in” or “to dwell with.” The point is not just that the land will be reinhabited, but that it will be in a relationship of “belonging” to the Israelites. Hence a relational verb like בָּעַל is used (J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah [NICOT], 2:581). Finally, “sons” is a well-known metaphor for “inhabitants” (J. de Waard, Isaiah, 208).
verses.commentary:
62:5 "virgin" All women in Israel/Judah were expected to be virgins when they married.

SPECIAL TOPIC: VIRGIN

▣

NASB, NKJV
"so your sons will marry you"

NRSV
"so shall your builder marry you"

TEV
"He who formed you will marry you"

NJB
"your rebuilder will wed you"

REB
"so will you be wedded to him who rebuilds you"

LXX
"so shall your son dwell with you"

Peshitta
"so shall your sons husband you"

By a revocalization of the consonants (בניך) "sons" (MT)
becomes "builder" (NRSV, JPSOA footnote, cf. Ps. 51:18; 102:16; 147:2), which fits the marriage imagery of
the strophe better. However, the UBS Text Project, p. 156, gives the MT "sons" an A rating. YHWH is the builder!

The LXX has a VERB that means "to dwell with."

The Expositor's Bible Commentary, vol. 1, p. 336, says of this verse

"Verse 5 presents as strange an analogy as that in Isa. 60:16. In both cases there seems
to be an intentional breach in the normal application of the analogy, perhaps in the interests of vivid impression.
Such analogies puzzle us, but we do not forget them!"

verses.zh: 耶路撒冷啊，我在你城上设立守望的，他们昼夜必不静默。呼吁耶和华的，你们不要歇息，
verses.en: I[NOTE:1] post watchmen on your walls, O Jerusalem;they should keep praying all day and all night.[NOTE:2] You who pray to[NOTE:3] the Lord, don’t be silent!
notes: The speaker here is probably the prophet.
Heb “all day and all night continually they do not keep silent.” The following lines suggest that they pray for the Lord’s intervention and restoration of the city.
verses.commentary:
62:6 "Watchmen" refers to the prophets (cf. Isa. 52:8; 56:10 [negated]; Jer. 6:17; Ezek. 3:17; 33:7), although the
rabbis see it referring to angels (cf. Dan. 4:13-17; Zech. 1:12-17).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANGELS IN THE BIBLE

62:6-7 "You who remind the Lord. . .give Him no rest until He establishes. . .Jerusalem"
This may refer to the theological truth that God has limited Himself to the prayers of His children (cf. James 4:2). It is
not overcoming the reluctance of an apathetic Deity, but it is the intercessory ministry of the people of God claiming
the promises of God.

The VERBS "appointed" and "remind" are both Hiphils.

SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERCESSORY PRAYER

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW GRAMMAR, II. B. #6

verses.zh: 也不要使他歇息，直等他建立耶路撒冷，使耶路撒冷在地上成为可赞美的。
verses.en: Don’t allow him to rest until he reestablishes Jerusalem,[NOTE:1] until he makes Jerusalem the pride[NOTE:2] of the earth.
notes: “Jerusalem” is supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons; note the following line.

verses.zh: 耶和华指着自己的右手和大能的膀臂起誓说：我必不再将你的五谷给你仇敌作食物；外邦人也不再喝你劳碌得来的新酒。
verses.en: The Lord swears an oath by his right hand,by his strong arm:[NOTE:1] “I will never again give your grain to your enemies as food,and foreigners will not drink your wine,which you worked hard to produce.
notes: The Lord’s right hand and strong arm here symbolize his power and remind the audience that his might guarantees the fulfillment of the following promise.
verses.commentary:
62:8 "The Lord has sworn by His right hand and by His strong arm" This is an
anthropomorphic phrase (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (anthropomorphism)). God does not have a body. He is Spirit
(cf. John 4:24), yet He swears by His own ability to act! YHWH is a God who has, will, and does act in individual lives, as well as nations.

YHWH's oath is a significant promise (cf. Isa. 54:9; Heb. 6:13-20; 7:20-28). It reminds us of

- the power of God's word, Isa. 55:11; 66:2d

- the trustworthy character of God, Isa. 45:22-23 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD [OT])

God has an eternal redemptive plan for all humans made in His image and likeness (cf. Acts 2:23; 3:18; 4:28; 1 Pet. 1:20, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN). The Suffering
Servant of Isa. 52:13-53:12 is the mechanism for universal redemption (cf. Rom. 5:12-21). The fellowship of Eden will be
restored for those who repent and believe in God's Messiah.

▣ "enemies. . .foreigners" This refers to the invasion of Palestine by foreigners. It is a direct reference
to the blessing versus cursing action of Lev. 26:16 and Deut. 28:30-33. Israel broke the Covenant. Israel suffered
the consequences. YHWH promises a future day when the blessings will be a reality (i.e. 1 Pet. 1:4).

Just a reminder, these are conditional promises. If Abraham's seed is faithful and obedient to YHWH's
covenant, blessing will flow. The purpose of these blessings is to reach the nations' attention so they can come to Him
and find peace, security, and abundance.

The unconditional promises are related to YHWH's promises regarding salvation and restoration, but
every individual must respond and continue to respond in an appropriate way (conditional covenant, see SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT).

- repentance (see SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE [OT])

- faith (see SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT)

- sevice

- obedience (see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)

- worship (see SPECIAL TOPIC: WORSHIP)

- perseverance (see SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSEVERANCE)

verses.zh: 惟有那收割的要吃，并赞美耶和华；那聚敛的要在我圣所的院内喝。
verses.en: “But those who harvest the grain[NOTE:1] will eat it,and will praise the Lord.Those who pick the grapes will drink the wine[NOTE:2] in the courts of my holy sanctuary.”
notes: Heb “it,” the grain mentioned in v. 8a.
Heb “and those who gather it will drink it.” The masculine singular pronominal suffixes attached to “gather” and “drink” refer back to the masculine noun תִּירוֹשׁ (tirosh, “wine”) in v. 8b.
verses.commentary:
62:9 "will drink it in the courts of My sanctuary" This refers to the fellowship meal between YHWH and
His covenant partner (cf. Deut. 12:18). These people are back in the land and the temple is restored.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE OFFERING

verses.zh: 你们当从门经过经过，预备百姓的路；修筑修筑大道，捡去石头，为万民竖立大旗，
verses.en: Come through! Come through the gates!Prepare the way for the people!Build it—build the roadway!Remove the stones.Lift a signal flag for the nations.
verses.commentary:
62:10-11 This is a message for the exiled people of God given by the prophet on YHWH's behalf. There is a
series of eight IMPERATIVES.

- go through ‒ Qal, BDB 716, KB 778

- go through ‒ same as #1

- clear the way ‒ Piel, BDB 815, KB 937

- build up ‒ Qal, BDB 699, KB 757

- build up ‒ same as #4 (repeating VERBS is a common way of emphasis in Isaiah)

- remove the stones ‒ Piel, BDB 709, KB 768

- lift up a standard ‒ Hiphil, BDB 926, KB 1202

- say ‒ Qal, BDB 55, KB 65

62:10 "go through the gates" This could refer to

- the gates of the cities of Mesopotamia where the Israelites and Judeans were exiled (esp. Babylon)

- the gates of the rebuilt (i.e. Cyrus II's decree in 538 B.C.)

- Jerusalem (Zerubbabel, Joshua, Ezra, Nehemiah)

- the temple

▣ "Clear the way for the people;

Build up, build up the highway"

This is common imagery of preparing the road for a royal visit (cf. Isa. 11:16; 19:23; 35:6-10; 40:3-4; 49:11; 57:14). This
is used several ways in the Bible.

- it is used of the return of the exiled

- it is used by John the Baptist as a self-designation of his own ministry (i.e. Isa. 40:3 quoted in Matt. 3:1-3)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

▣ "lift up a standard" This refers to the flag of a tribe or military unit. Notice here the standard
is over "the peoples" and Isa. 62:11a "to the end of the earth." The insignia of Israel is now the flag of all who
believe, receive, and acknowledge YHWH (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 12:4-5; 25:6-9; 42:6-12; 45:22-23; 49:5-6; 51:4-5; 56:6-7; 60:1-3: 66:23).

verses.zh: 看哪，耶和华曾宣告到地极，对锡安的居民（原文是女子）说：你的拯救者来到。他的赏赐在他那里；他的报应在他面前。
verses.en: Look, the Lord announces to the entire earth:[NOTE:1] “Say to Daughter Zion,‘Look, your deliverer comes!Look, his reward is with him,and his reward goes before him!’”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “to the end of the earth” (so NASB, NRSV).
As v. 12 indicates, the returning exiles are the Lord’s reward/prize. See also 40:10 and the note there.
verses.commentary:
62:11 "to the end of the earth" It is this universal aspect of YHWH's promises that signal that His love
and salvation are for all humans, not just Israel. Please look at the important Special Topic below!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "Say. . ." There are three truths to be spoken (Qal IMPERATIVES) by the
prophet about YHWH's coming (cf. Isa. 40:3) in blessing.

- your salvation comes (cf. Isa. 49:6)

- His reward is with Him

- His recompense before Him (cf. Isa. 40:10)

verses.zh: 人必称他们为「圣民」，为「耶和华的赎民」；你也必称为「被眷顾、不撇弃的城」。
verses.en: They will be called, “The Holy People,the Ones Protected[NOTE:1] by the Lord.”You will be called, “Sought After,City Not Abandoned.”
notes: Or “the redeemed of the Lord” (KJV, NAB).
verses.commentary:
62:12 "they will call them" This is an allusion to "the new name" of Isa. 62:2. The non-Israelites
will now call them, not "Forsaken" or "Desolate" (Isa. 62:4), but

- the holy people

- the redeemed of the Lord

- sought out

▣ "The redeemed of the Lord" "Redeemed" (BDB 145 I) is related to the
concept of Go'el. This was the kinsman redeemer who bought back his relative from poverty or capture.
YHWH as a go'el is another example of Deity described in close intimate personal family terms.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

▣ "Sought out, a city not forsaken" This title was very significant because it states the truth that
God was not running from the covenant people but running toward them!

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You,
the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Does Isaiah 62 refer only to the Exile or is it a typology referring to the reign of the Messiah?

- Define the OT terms "righteousness" and "salvation."

- Why does God have to be reminded in Isa. 62:6 of His promises?

- Does God have a special love for Israel that He does not have for other nations?

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS ‒ Isaiah 60-62 is a literary unit and should be read and interpreted together.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 62:1-5

1For Zion's sake I will not keep silent,

And for Jerusalem's sake I will not keep quiet,

Until her righteousness goes forth like brightness,

And her salvation like a torch that is burning.

2The nations will see your righteousness,

And all kings your glory;

And you will be called by a new name

Which the mouth of the Lord will designate.

3You will also be a crown of beauty in the hand of the Lord ,

And a royal diadem in the hand of your God.

4It will no longer be said to you, "Forsaken,"

Nor to your land will it any longer be said, "Desolate"

But you will be called, "My delight is in her,"

And your land, "Married";

For the Lord delights in you,

And to Him your land will be married.

5For as a young man marries a virgin,

So your sons will marry you;

And as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride,

So your God will rejoice over you.
